appraisal_events.evidence: « J’étais libre, mais je ne serais pas venue [...] ce n’est plus qu’une ruine. Et puis je déteste les vers de Carmen Sylva [...] Voilà où elle est incomparable. » Alix supporta le coup sans faiblir [...] une joue s’écaillait [...] Peut-être un hiver de plus la jetterait bas.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Villeparisis rebuffs Alix's boastful anecdote about Ristori and Carmen Sylva, refusing the implied invitation and asserting superior taste and connections; the narrator explicitly frames this as a 'blow' Alix must withstand, immediately followed by an unflattering description of Alix's physical decay.

status_effects.explanation: Alix is decisively bested in the social exchange, forced to absorb Mme de Villeparisis's dismissive rebuttal without effective reply.
The narrator's description of Alix's marble rigidity and visible physical decay immediately following the exchange casts her in an unflattering, declining light.
Mme de Villeparisis wins the exchange, displaying superior discernment, connections (the duchesse d'Aoste), and control over the conversation, which she then redirects at will.

ambiguities: The unnamed speaker ('elle') of the opening remarks about Mme de Luynes and Mme Ristori is identified as Alix only by the later sentence 'Alix supporta le coup sans faiblir'; this identification is treated as certain but relies on that later naming.
